plain.en: the share of a group that had the exposure

means.en: In a case-control table, the share exposed among the cases, a/(a+c), or among the controls, b/(b+d). Each rate divides by its own column total.
A result small enough that chance alone would rarely produce it. The usual cut-off is a P value below 0.05, and it says nothing about whether the comparison was fair.

plain.en: the chance of a gap this big by luck

means.en: The chance of seeing a gap at least as large as the one observed if exposure and disease had no link. It measures chance only, never bias and never causation.
The odds of exposure among the cases divided by the odds among the controls, ad/bc. It estimates the relative risk fairly only when the disease is rare.

plain.en: risk in the exposed divided by risk in the unexposed

means.en: A ratio of two incidences, so it needs a cohort followed forward. A case-control study cannot measure it directly and reports an odds ratio instead.

plain.en: a third feature travelling with the exposure

means.en: A feature that is linked to both the exposure and the disease and can create the whole apparent effect, as age does in many studies. Matching cases and controls on it removes the distortion.

plain.en: new cases over a set time among people at risk

means.en: The number of new cases in a period divided by the population at risk. A case-control study cannot measure it, because it never follows a group forward.

plain.en: a systematic error built into the study

means.en: An error created by how the groups were chosen or questioned, not by chance. It pushes the estimate in one direction, and no sample size or P value repairs it.
People with the disease search their memory for the exposure more carefully than people without it, so exposed cases are over-counted and the odds ratio climbs.

plain.en: the questioner digs harder into one group

means.en: An interviewer who knows the hypothesis probes the cases' answers more searchingly than the controls' and records more exposure among the cases. Comparing interview lengths is a direct check.

plain.en: the door into the study picks a tilted sample

means.en: The chosen cases and controls stop representing the populations they came from, because the door that let them in (hospital admission, employment records) admits different kinds of people at different rates.

plain.en: the hospital door manufactures an association

means.en: When the exposure and the disease each raise the chance of hospital admission, the hospital's own patients can show an association that the population behind the hospital does not have. No matching removes it.

plain.en: a group that shares one experience in one period

means.en: A group of people who share one characteristic or experience within a defined time period - all born in 2010, all exposed to one drug, all married in the same year. A cohort study follows such a group forward to count who falls ill.

plain.en: a study that starts before the outcomes have happened

means.en: A cohort study whose investigation begins while the disease outcomes still lie ahead, so it watches them occur. The chapter also calls it a 'current' cohort study.

plain.en: a study that starts after the outcomes are already on record

means.en: A cohort study whose outcomes have all occurred before the investigation begins. The investigator goes back in time, sometimes 10 to 30 years, picks the groups from old employment, medical or other records, and traces them forward to the present; also called a 'historical' cohort study.

plain.en: people slipping out of a study while it runs

means.en: The loss of study members during follow-up, through death, moving away or refusal to continue. A cohort is practical when attrition can be minimised, because every loss thins the denominators the analysis needs.

A painful condition in which the joints of the spine stiffen. Between 1934 and 1954 it was often treated with large doses of radiation therapy, which is how the Court-Brown and Doll cohort could be picked out of treatment records years later.
A heart attack: a patch of heart muscle dies when its blood supply is cut off. Everyone who survived one in a particular year can form a cohort.

plain.en: the death of a newborn baby

means.en: The death of a baby in the weeks around the birth. It was the outcome counted in the Boston foetal-monitoring study, and it follows each birth within days or weeks.
